topics.title: Rhetoric and argumentation
topics.description: Parallel structures, hedges, and the rhythm of formal Chinese

guide.intro: Mandarin formal writing has a rhythm. It loves parallel pairs, four-character cadences, and concessive hedges that English would handle with one comma. Internalizing these patterns is what separates the C1 essay ("correct") from the C2 essay ("this could be in 人民日報").

sections.text: Parallel pair: 一方面…另一方面…
"On one hand…on the other…" The skeleton of every balanced opinion piece. The two clauses should be the same length and grammatical shape — that's where Chinese rhetoric earns its style points.

rows.source: 一方面 我們要發展經濟，另一方面 也要保護環境。
rows.pinyin: Yì fāngmiàn wǒmen yào fāzhǎn jīngjì, lìng yì fāngmiàn yě yào bǎohù huánjìng.
rows.translation: On one hand we must grow the economy; on the other, we must also protect the environment.

sections.text: Concessive: …也好，…也罷
"Whether X or Y — either way…" A literary, faintly resigned tone. You'll see it in op-eds and novelistic narration. The pair must mirror — same word class, similar length.

rows.source: 成功 也好，失敗 也罷，過程 才 重要。
rows.pinyin: Chénggōng yě hǎo, shībài yě bà, guòchéng cái zhòngyào.
rows.translation: Success or failure — what matters is the process.

rows.source: 你 信 也好，不信 也罷，事實 就 在 那裡。
rows.pinyin: Nǐ xìn yě hǎo, bú xìn yě bà, shìshí jiù zài nàlǐ.
rows.translation: Believe it or not, the facts are right there.

sections.text: Choice and preference: 與其…不如… / 寧可…也不…
Two paired patterns for ranking options. 與其 X 不如 Y — "rather than X, better Y." 寧可 X 也不 Y — "would rather X than Y." Both are written-register; both make the speaker sound deliberative.

rows.source: 與其 抱怨，不如 行動。
rows.translation: Rather than complain, take action.

rows.source: 他 寧可 辭職，也不 妥協。
rows.pinyin: Tā nìngkě cízhí, yě bù tuǒxié.
rows.translation: He would rather quit than compromise.

sections.text: Discourse shift: 倒是
倒是 (dào shì) — "on the contrary / actually / as it happens." A discourse marker that signals a gentle reversal of expectation. Not the dramatic 反而 — softer, more conversational-formal.

rows.source: 他 平時 話 不多，關鍵 時刻 倒是 很 果斷。
rows.pinyin: Tā píngshí huà bù duō, guānjiàn shíkè dàoshì hěn guǒduàn.
rows.translation: He's usually quiet, but at critical moments he's actually very decisive.

rows.source: 你 這麼 一 說，我 倒是 想起來 了。
rows.pinyin: Nǐ zhème yì shuō, wǒ dàoshì xiǎng qǐlái le.
rows.translation: Now that you mention it, I do remember.

sections.text: Building from a premise: 既然…就…
"Given that X, then Y." The premise is treated as agreed-upon — it shifts the conversation forward. Distinct from 因為…所以… (causal) and 如果…就… (hypothetical).

rows.source: 既然 你 已經 決定 了，就 別 再 猶豫。
rows.pinyin: Jìrán nǐ yǐjīng juédìng le, jiù bié zài yóuyù.
rows.translation: Since you've already decided, stop hesitating.

sections.text: Cause-and-effect chain: 之所以…是因為…
"The reason X is because Y." Stylistically inverted from English — Chinese leads with the consequence and only later names the cause. Beloved by editorialists building suspense.

rows.source: 他 之所以 成功，是 因為 他 從 不 放棄。
rows.pinyin: Tā zhī suǒyǐ chénggōng, shì yīnwèi tā cóng bù fàngqì.
rows.translation: The reason he succeeded is that he never gives up.

sections.text: Four-character rhythm rule: when in doubt, balance. 不僅…而且… is fine; 不僅 simple, 而且 ornate sounds wrong. Match the weight of the two clauses and your sentence will sound native.

lessons.title: Parallel pairs
lessons.description: 一方面 / 另一方面 and rhythmic balance

exercises.prompt: Build: "On one hand we must develop the economy, on the other we must protect the environment."
exercises.answer: 一方面 我們 要 發展 經濟 另一方面 也 要 保護 環境

exercises.prompt: Which sentence has the most balanced rhetorical rhythm?
options: 一方面要兼顧效率，另一方面要切實地保障社會公平。
一方面要兼顧效率，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要努力兼顧效率問題，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要兼顧整體效率，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.answer: 一方面要兼顧效率，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.explanation: All four are grammatical; only the answer keeps both clauses at the same length and shape (要 + 2-char verb + 2-char abstract object). The others pad one side — "切實地保障社會公平," "努力兼顧效率問題," "兼顧整體效率" — breaking the parallel weight Chinese editorials chase.

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a parallel construction. Which of these has the cleanest balanced rhythm?
exercises.spokenText: 一方面要發展經濟，另一方面要保護環境
options: 一方面要發展經濟，另一方面要保護環境
一方面要發展經濟，另一方面也要切實地保護好我們的生態環境
一方面經濟，另一方面環境
一方面要發展，另一方面我們必須立即推進環境保護工作
exercises.answer: 一方面要發展經濟，另一方面要保護環境
exercises.explanation: Both clauses: 要 + 2-char verb + 2-char object. Same syllable count, same shape. The padded options break the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Build a long balanced parallel: "On one hand we must heed people's hopes; on the other we must respond to people's worries."
exercises.answer: 一方面 我們 要 傾聽 民意 另一方面 我們 要 回應 民憂

exercises.prompt: the parallel pattern to its essay function

pairs.right: Not only X but also Y — escalation
Either X or Y — listing alternatives

exercises.prompt: Which sentence shows the strongest 4-character cadence balance?
options: 我們要重視效率，同時也要顧及到公平問題
效率是重要的，公平也是重要的
我們應當兼顧效率和公平這兩個方面
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with parallel grammar (noun + verb + noun's role). Editorial cadence at its tightest. The other options say the same thing but lose the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Complete the balanced pair: "成功 ___ 失敗 ___ 過程 才 重要." (Fill the two concessive markers.)
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罷 — "whether X or Y, either way…" Literary concessive pair. Both halves must be matched in length.

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a long compound sentence. Pick the version with the most balanced parallel rhythm.
exercises.spokenText: 教育之於個人，關乎前途；教育之於國家，關乎未來
options: 教育之於個人，關乎前途；教育之於國家，關乎未來
教育對個人來說是關於前途的事情；教育對國家來說則關乎未來
教育對個人有影響；教育對國家也很重要
教育之於個人關乎前途，對國家來說關乎未來這一重要議題
exercises.answer: 教育之於個人，關乎前途；教育之於國家，關乎未來
exercises.explanation: Two clauses, perfectly mirrored: 教育 之於 X，關乎 Y. Same length, same shape, classical 之於 as the connector. The distractors all break the symmetry.

exercises.prompt: Why does Chinese formal writing chase clause-length balance more aggressively than English?
options: Chinese has no other rhythm — it's impossible to write without it
Cultural-rhetorical convention rooted in classical 駢文 (parallel prose) — balanced rhythm signals seriousness and care
Editors enforce it via word counts
exercises.answer: Cultural-rhetorical convention rooted in classical 駢文 (parallel prose) — balanced rhythm signals seriousness and care
exercises.explanation: 駢文 (parallel prose) trained centuries of writers to value matched clauses. Modern editorial Chinese inherits the instinct: balanced rhythm = serious writer. Imbalanced clauses sound rushed even when grammatically fine.

exercises.answer: efficiency first, fairness at the root
acceptableAnswers: efficiency comes first, fairness is foundational
exercises.explanation: Four-character + four-character — the editorial signature rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Build the rhythm: "___ 方面 我們 要 傾聽 民意，___ 方面 我們 要 回應 民憂." Fill the parallel openers.
exercises.explanation: 一方面…另一方面… is the two-sided framing pattern. Both halves must be matched in clause length.

exercises.prompt: Which line keeps the tightest 4+4 cadence?
options: 我們要兼顧經濟發展和環境保護這兩件大事
經濟發展，環境保護，都很重要
我們既要發展也要保護
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character parallel clauses; identical verb-object grammar. Editorial rhythm at its most compressed.

exercises.prompt: Build a tight 4+4 parallel: "Develop the economy; protect the environment."
exercises.answer: 發展 經濟 保護 環境

exercises.prompt: the cadence to the editorial effect
Which version has the strongest parallel rhythm?
options: 效率比較重要，公平也得照顧到
我們應該兼顧效率和公平
效率是先要的，公平要作為根本

exercises.source: 教育之於國家，關乎未來
exercises.answer: education, to a nation, concerns its future
acceptableAnswers: for a nation, education is its future
education matters to the nation's future
exercises.explanation: 之於 = formal "with respect to." The line mirrors a preceding one about 教育之於個人.

exercises.prompt: Mirror the editorial pair: "教育 之 於 個人，關乎 前途；教育 之 ___ 國家，關乎 未來." Fill the formal preposition (one character).
exercises.explanation: 之於 — literary "with respect to."

exercises.prompt: Which line below is the LEAST balanced for an editorial?
options: 我們應當兼顧整體效率，也要關心一下公平的問題
exercises.answer: 我們應當兼顧整體效率，也要關心一下公平的問題
exercises.explanation: Mismatched clause lengths and softeners (一下) break the editorial cadence.

exercises.prompt: Build a literary parallel pair: "Listen to the people's hopes; respond to the people's worries."
exercises.answer: 傾聽 民意 回應 民憂

lessons.title: 也好 / 也罷 — concessive shrug
lessons.description: Either way, the point stands

exercises.prompt: 成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才重要。
options: Success matters more than the process
Win or lose, what matters is the journey
Failure is the mother of success
Don't try and you can't fail
exercises.answer: Win or lose, what matters is the journey

exercises.prompt: Build: "Believe it or not, the facts are right there."
exercises.answer: 你 信 也好 不信 也罷 事實 就 在 那裡

exercises.prompt: What register does …也好，…也罷 belong to?
exercises.explanation: It carries a slightly resigned, philosophical tone. You hear it in newspaper columns and literary fiction, rarely in casual chat.

exercises.prompt: the C2-register connector pattern to what it does

pairs.right: Whether X or Y, either way…
The reason X is that Y

exercises.prompt: Build a long concessive sentence: "Whether the policy is finally adopted or rejected, public discussion has already gone deep."
exercises.answer: 政策 通過 也好 否決 也罷 公共 討論 已 走 向 深入

exercises.prompt: A columnist reads a literary concessive line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才是真正的財富
options: 成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才是真正的財富
成功或者失敗都沒關係，過程才重要
不管是成功還是失敗，過程是關鍵
無論成功失敗，過程是真財富
exercises.answer: 成功也好，失敗也罷，過程才是真正的財富
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罷 + 才是 + multi-character noun phrase carries the literary register. The distractors paraphrase the same idea in everyday or semi-formal Chinese.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence misuses 也好…也罷?
options: 信也好，不信也罷，事實就在那裡
成功也好，失敗也罷，過程最重要
他來也好，沒來也罷，會議照常
天氣也好，所以我去散步
exercises.answer: 天氣也好，所以我去散步
exercises.explanation: Here 也好 means "is fine" (modern adjective use), not the concessive pair. The pattern 也好…也罷 requires two contrasting alternatives — option 4 has only one and is using 也好 in a totally different sense.

exercises.prompt: An op-ed reads: "贊 ___ ，罵 ___ ，時間 終 會 給出 答案." Fill the two concessive markers.
exercises.explanation: 贊也好，罵也罷 — "praise or scold, either way…" Two 1-character verbs balanced perfectly under the concessive frame.

exercises.prompt: the concessive pattern to its register subtlety

pairs.right: Highly classical — "even if X, still Y"

exercises.prompt: 贏也好，輸也罷，他都已經走得太遠。
exercises.hint: In this novelistic line, what does the 也好…也罷 contribute?
options: A weary, fatalistic tone — outcome no longer matters
exercises.answer: A weary, fatalistic tone — outcome no longer matters
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罷 carries a faintly resigned quality that's perfect for a novelist signaling that a character has passed the point of caring about outcomes. That tonal coloring is what separates it from the neutral 無論…還是….
也好…也罷 — slightly weary, philosophical concessive pair.

exercises.prompt: Build the concessive pair: "贊 ___，罵 ___，時間 終 會 給出 答案." (Fill the two markers.)
exercises.explanation: 贊也好，罵也罷 — "praise or scold, either way…"

exercises.prompt: Which sentence misuses the concessive pair 也好…也罷?
options: 信也好，不信也罷，事實就在那裡
他來也好，沒來也罷，會議照常
天氣也好，所以我去散步
成功也好，失敗也罷，過程最重要
exercises.answer: 天氣也好，所以我去散步
exercises.explanation: 也好 here is the modern adjective "is fine," not the concessive marker — and the pattern needs two balanced alternatives.

exercises.prompt: Build a literary concessive: "Whether praised or scolded, time will give the answer."
exercises.answer: 贊 也好 罵 也罷 時間 終 會 給出 答案

exercises.prompt: the concessive to its tonal coloring
A columnist reads a literary concessive. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 信也好，不信也罷，事實就在那裡
options: 信也好，不信也罷，事實就在那裡
你信不信，事實都在那兒
無論你信不信，事實擺在那裡
不管你信不信，事實都擺著
exercises.answer: 信也好，不信也罷，事實就在那裡

exercises.explanation: Used alone, 也罷 means "so be it"; in pairs (也好…也罷), it carries half the concessive frame.

exercises.prompt: Concessive line: "政策 通過 也好，否決 ___ ，公共 討論 已 走 向 深入." (one character + 罷)
exercises.explanation: 通過也好，否決也罷 — "passed or rejected, either way…"

exercises.prompt: What kind of speaker most likely uses 也好…也罷?
options: A columnist or novelist signaling weary detachment
exercises.answer: A columnist or novelist signaling weary detachment
exercises.explanation: Its slightly resigned, philosophical coloring suits literary op-ed and novel-narrator prose.

exercises.prompt: Build (literary novelistic): "Whether he wins or loses, he has already gone too far."
exercises.answer: 贏 也好 輸 也罷 他 都 已經 走 得 太 遠

lessons.title: 之所以…是因為…
lessons.description: Lead with the consequence, end with the cause

exercises.prompt: Build: "The reason he succeeded is that he never gives up."
exercises.answer: 他 之所以 成功 是因為 他 從不 放棄

exercises.prompt: Why might a writer prefer 之所以…是因為… over 因為…所以…?
options: It foregrounds the result and makes the cause feel like a reveal
It is grammatically required after 但是
exercises.answer: It foregrounds the result and makes the cause feel like a reveal
exercises.explanation: Inverting the order is a rhetorical move — it lets the writer build small suspense before naming the cause.

exercises.prompt: "既然你已經決定了，___ 別再猶豫。" — fill the blank.
exercises.explanation: 既然…就… is the fixed pair. Both halves carry the conclusion forward.

exercises.prompt: Build a long causal-reveal sentence: "The reason this reform has succeeded is precisely that it places the people's livelihood first."
exercises.answer: 這 項 改革 之所以 成功 正是 因為 它 把 民生 放在 首位

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads an inverted causal sentence. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 他之所以堅持下來，是因為他從未忘記最初的承諾
options: 他之所以堅持下來，是因為他從未忘記最初的承諾
他堅持下來是因為他沒忘記最初的承諾
因為他沒忘記承諾，所以他堅持下來了
他從未忘記承諾，所以他堅持下來
exercises.answer: 他之所以堅持下來，是因為他從未忘記最初的承諾
exercises.explanation: 之所以…是因為… is the essay-style inversion (lead with consequence, reveal the cause). The other three express the same idea in 因為…所以… or modern colloquial frames.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之所以 INCORRECTLY?
options: 他之所以成功，是因為堅持
她之所以離開，是因為身體原因
我之所以喜歡，是因為它很美
之所以下雨，今天不出門
exercises.answer: 之所以下雨，今天不出門
exercises.explanation: 之所以 must attach to a clause as the consequence ("the reason X is…"), and is then completed by 是因為 + cause. Option 4 misuses it as a stand-in for 因為. The other three are well-formed 之所以…是因為… inversions.

exercises.prompt: Complete the inversion: "中國 經濟 之所以 能夠 持續 增長，___ 改革開放 政策 的 推動." Fill the cause-marker (3 characters).
exercises.explanation: 之所以…是因為… is the fixed inverted pair. The cause clause (改革開放政策的推動) follows 是因為 as the rhetorical reveal.

exercises.prompt: the causal connector to its register
這家公司之所以失去市場，是因為它忘記了使用者。
exercises.hint: What rhetorical effect does leading with 之所以 have?
options: It builds suspense — the failure is named first; the cause becomes the reveal
exercises.answer: It builds suspense — the failure is named first; the cause becomes the reveal
exercises.explanation: 因為…所以… presents cause then effect; 之所以…是因為… inverts to lead with effect. The inversion turns the cause into a punchline — exactly what columnists want for impact.

exercises.prompt: Build a premise sentence (既然…就…): "Since the people have given their trust, then we must repay them with effort."
exercises.answer: 既然 人民 給予 我們 信任 我們 就 應當 以 努力 回報
the reason X is that Y
acceptableAnswers: X is the case because Y
the reason for X is Y
exercises.explanation: Inverted causal: result first, cause as reveal.

exercises.prompt: Inversion: "中國 經濟 ___ 能 持續 增長，是 因為 改革開放 的 推動." (3 characters)
exercises.explanation: 之所以 leads with the result; 是因為 follows with the cause.

exercises.prompt: Why might a writer choose 之所以…是因為… over 因為…所以…?
options: It foregrounds the result and turns the cause into a reveal
It is required after 但是
exercises.answer: It foregrounds the result and turns the cause into a reveal
exercises.explanation: Inverting cause and effect builds rhetorical suspense — perfect for editorials.

exercises.prompt: Build: "The reason he persisted is that he never forgot the original promise."
exercises.answer: 他 之所以 堅持 下來 是因為 他 從未 忘記 最初 的 承諾

exercises.prompt: the causal connector to its register
A speaker reads an inverted causal line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 這項改革之所以成功，是因為它把民生放在首位
options: 這項改革之所以成功，是因為它把民生放在首位
改革成功的原因是把人民生活放第一
因為重視民生，改革就成功了
改革靠的是把民生放第一
exercises.answer: 這項改革之所以成功，是因為它把民生放在首位

exercises.explanation: 由於…故… is the most formal of the causal patterns — closest to classical.

exercises.prompt: Premise: "___ 你 已 決定，就 別 再 猶豫." Fill the literary premise marker (2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 既然…就… — "since X (premise), then Y."

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 之所以 INCORRECTLY?
options: 他 之所以 成功 是因為 堅持
她 之所以 離開 是因為 健康
之所以 下雨 今天 不 出門
我 之所以 喜歡 是因為 它 美
exercises.answer: 之所以 下雨 今天 不 出門
exercises.explanation: 之所以 must attach to a clause as the result; 是因為 introduces the cause. Used alone for 因為, it is wrong.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Since the people have given us their trust, we must repay them with effort."
exercises.answer: 既然 人民 給予 我們 信任 我們 就 應當 以 努力 回報

lessons.title: Choice, preference, and 倒是
lessons.description: 與其…不如, 寧可…也不, and the discourse marker 倒是

exercises.prompt: 與其抱怨，不如行動。
exercises.hint: What does the 與其…不如… structure express?
options: A preference: rather than X, better Y
exercises.answer: A preference: rather than X, better Y
exercises.explanation: 與其 (yǔqí) sets up the dispreferred option; 不如 (bùrú) names what's better. The whole pattern is a deliberative comparison.

exercises.prompt: 他寧可辭職，也不妥協。
exercises.hint: What does the 寧可…也不 pattern signal about the speaker?
options: Strongly prefers the first option, rejecting the second
exercises.answer: Strongly prefers the first option, rejecting the second
exercises.explanation: 寧可…也不 — "would rather X than Y." The first clause is what the speaker chooses; the second is what they refuse, even at cost.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Rather than complain, it's better to take action."
exercises.answer: 與其 抱怨 不如 行動

exercises.prompt: 他平時話不多，關鍵時刻倒是很果斷。
exercises.hint: What does 倒是 contribute here?
options: It introduces a gentle reversal of expectation — "actually / on the contrary"
exercises.answer: It introduces a gentle reversal of expectation — "actually / on the contrary"
exercises.explanation: 倒是 (dàoshì) is a soft contrastive — softer than 反而, conversational-formal. It signals that despite what one might expect, the opposite is true.

exercises.prompt: "你這麼一說，我 ___ 想起來了." Fill the discourse marker that means "actually / now that you mention it."
exercises.explanation: 倒是 (or just 倒) marks the gentle realization — your remark caused an unexpected memory.

exercises.prompt: Build a long deliberative sentence: "He would rather sacrifice short-term profit than betray the trust of his customers."
exercises.answer: 他 寧可 犧牲 短期 利益 也不 辜負 客戶 的 信任

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions. Pick the one with the cleanest 與其…不如… cadence.
exercises.spokenText: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
options: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
與其在那裡坐著空談道理，不如起來就趕緊去行動
與其討論，不如行動起來積極地解決問題
與其坐下來談論各種道理，不如行動
exercises.answer: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with mirrored grammar (verb 而 verb-object). Classical-flavored balance — the C2 essay closer. The padded distractors lose the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: the choice/preference pattern to its rhetorical use

pairs.right: Recommending the better of two options
Strong preference, refusing the alternative at cost

exercises.prompt: Which captures the difference between 倒是 and 反而 most accurately?
options: 倒是 is sharper than 反而
倒是 is softer / more conversational; 反而 is sharper, often signaling unexpected counter-result
反而 is colloquial and 倒是 is rude
exercises.answer: 倒是 is softer / more conversational; 反而 is sharper, often signaling unexpected counter-result
exercises.explanation: 倒是 is a gentle reversal ("actually / as it happens"); 反而 marks a stronger, often surprising counter-result. C2 readers feel the difference instantly.

exercises.prompt: Complete the proverb-style line: "___ 抱怨 命運 不公 ， ___ 改寫 自己 的 故事." Fill the deliberative pair (2 + 2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 與其抱怨命運不公，不如改寫自己的故事 — "rather than complain about an unfair fate, better to rewrite your own story." Classic motivational rhetoric in deliberative cadence.

exercises.answer: rather than complain, better to act
exercises.explanation: 與其…不如… — the deliberative comparison.

exercises.prompt: Deliberative: "___ 抱怨 命運 不公，___ 改寫 自己 的 故事." Fill the pair (2 + 2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 與其抱怨…，不如改寫… — motivational rhetoric.

exercises.prompt: 他 寧可 辭職，也不 妥協
options: He would rather resign than compromise
exercises.answer: He would rather resign than compromise
exercises.explanation: 寧可…也不 — strong preference, refusing the alternative at cost.

exercises.prompt: Build (literary): "Rather than sit and debate the way, better to rise and walk it."
exercises.answer: 與其 坐 而 論 道 不如 起 而 行 之

exercises.prompt: the choice/preference pattern to its use
A literary line is read. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
options: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
與其坐著討論，不如起來行動
exercises.answer: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之

exercises.explanation: Soft contrastive — gentler than 反而.

exercises.prompt: Reversal: "你 這麼 一 說，我 ___ 想 起來 了." Fill the soft contrastive (2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 倒是 — marks an unexpected memory or admission.

exercises.prompt: How does 倒是 differ from 反而?
options: 倒是 is sharper than 反而
倒是 is softer / conversational; 反而 is sharper and often signals an unexpected counter-result
exercises.answer: 倒是 is softer / conversational; 反而 is sharper and often signals an unexpected counter-result
exercises.explanation: Both are contrastives but with different rhetorical force.

exercises.prompt: Build: "He would rather sacrifice short-term gain than betray his customers' trust."
exercises.answer: 他 寧可 犧牲 短期 利益 也不 辜負 客戶 的 信任

lessons.title: Dialogue: Editing an op-ed
lessons.description: A journalist defends rhetorical choices to a sharp editor.

exercises.prompt: Op-ed revision with the senior editor

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 稿子我看了，開篇用了排比，氣勢是有的。(gǎo zi wǒ kàn le, kāi piān yòng le pái bǐ, qì shì shì yǒu de.)
turns.spokenText: 稿子我看了，開篇用了排比，氣勢是有的。

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 但第二段「政策如春風，似細雨，若朝陽」——這是哪種修辭？(dàn dì èr duàn zhèng cè rú chūn fēng, sì xì yǔ, ruò zhāo yáng — zhè shì nǎ zhǒng xiū cí?)
turns.spokenText: 但第二段「政策如春風，似細雨，若朝陽」——這是哪種修辭？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Name the figure used by the writer.
options: 排比 + 比喻 (pái bǐ + bǐ yù – parallelism with simile)
turns.answer: 排比 + 比喻 (pái bǐ + bǐ yù – parallelism with simile)

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 不錯。但第三段那句反問，未免太重，讀者會覺得說教。(bù cuò. dàn dì sān duàn nà jù fǎn wèn, wèi miǎn tài zhòng, dú zhě huì jué de shuō jiào.)
turns.spokenText: 不錯。但第三段那句反問，未免太重，讀者會覺得說教。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Choose the most diplomatic professional reply.
options: 我改成陳述句，留一分餘地。(wǒ gǎi chéng chén shù jù, liú yī fēn yú dì.)
隨便你，反正我懶得改。(suí biàn nǐ, fǎn zhèng wǒ lǎn de gǎi.)
你不懂修辭。(nǐ bù dǒng xiū cí.)
這有什麼好挑的？(zhè yǒu shén me hǎo tiāo de?)
turns.answer: 我改成陳述句，留一分餘地。(wǒ gǎi chéng chén shù jù, liú yī fēn yú dì.)

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 好。結尾「不可不察也」——這「也」是古意還是口語？(hǎo. jié wěi bù kě bù chá yě — zhè yě shì gǔ yì hái shì kǒu yǔ?)
turns.spokenText: 好。結尾「不可不察也」——這「也」是古意還是口語？

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Which register is 「不可不察也」?
turns.answer: Classical/literary — sentence-final assertion marker

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 正是。社論結尾用它，分量自重。(zhèng shì. shè lùn jié wěi yòng tā, fèn liàng zì zhòng.)
turns.spokenText: 正是。社論結尾用它，分量自重。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill the connector for "yet/and so" in: 富___不驕 (rich yet not arrogant).
turns.answer: 而

turns.speaker: zhao
turns.text: 「富而不驕」——好句子。明早九點見報。(fù ér bù jiāo — hǎo jù zi. míng zǎo jiǔ diǎn jiàn bào.)
turns.spokenText: 「富而不驕」——好句子。明早九點見報。

exercises.explanation: 排比 — the rhetorical figure of three or more parallel clauses.

exercises.prompt: Editorial rhetoric: "政策 ___ 春 風，似 細 雨，若 朝 陽." Fill the literary "is like" (one character).
exercises.hint: Three simile markers in a row.
exercises.explanation: 如…似…若… — three near-synonyms for "like" stacked for cadence.

exercises.prompt: 「政策如春風，似細雨，若朝陽」用了什麼修辭？
options: 排比 + 比喻 — parallelism with simile
exercises.answer: 排比 + 比喻 — parallelism with simile
exercises.explanation: Three parallel clauses (排比), each a simile (比喻). Classic editorial flourish.

exercises.prompt: Build the editorial figure: "Policy is like spring wind, like fine rain, like the rising sun."
exercises.answer: 政策 如 春風 似 細雨 若 朝陽

exercises.prompt: the rhetorical figure to its Chinese name
An editor names a rhetorical figure. Pick what you hear.

exercises.explanation: 未免 — "can hardly avoid" → a softened critique.

exercises.prompt: Editor diplomacy: "我 改 成 陳 述 句，留 一 分 ___." Fill the closing word (2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 留餘地 — leave room (for the reader's own thought). An editor's standard counsel.

exercises.prompt: 「不可不察也」中的「也」是什麼用法？
exercises.explanation: 也 here anchors the assertion — "is certainly the case." Survives in editorial closes.

exercises.prompt: Build the diplomatic response: "I'll change it to a declarative — leave a little room."
exercises.answer: 我 改 成 陳述句 留 一 分 餘地

exercises.prompt: the editor's phrase to its meaning
An editor closes a meeting. Pick what you hear.

exercises.explanation: Adversative 而 — "X yet not Y."

exercises.prompt: Adversative connector: "富 ___ 不 驕." (one character)
exercises.explanation: 而 — the adversative literary connector. 但 is its colloquial cousin.

exercises.prompt: 稿子開篇用了排比，氣勢是有的。
exercises.hint: What did the editor just say?
options: The opening used parallelism — there's force, alright
exercises.answer: The opening used parallelism — there's force, alright
exercises.explanation: 排比 = parallelism; 氣勢 = momentum / force. The editor concedes the piece has it.

exercises.prompt: Build: "The piece's opening used parallelism — there's force, alright."
exercises.answer: 稿子 開篇 用 了 排比 氣勢 是 有 的

exercises.prompt: each editor's verdict to its underlying meaning

exercises.explanation: 說教 — the editor's complaint about a heavy rhetorical question.

exercises.prompt: An editor calls a paragraph "說教" — what should the writer do?
options: Soften the moralizing tone, perhaps convert to a declarative
exercises.answer: Soften the moralizing tone, perhaps convert to a declarative
exercises.explanation: 說教 = preachy. The fix is to dial down rhetorical questions and let the reader draw the conclusion.

topics.title: 成語 and 歇後語 mastery
topics.description: Higher-tier idioms plus the two-part allegorical sayings of everyday speech

lessons.title: Higher-tier 成語
lessons.description: Six idioms that mark you as a serious reader

exercises.prompt: the 成語 to its meaning
Your team raises 1% of what is needed for disaster relief. A reporter writes: "這點捐款無異於___。" Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 杯水車薪 = a cup of water on a burning cartload — the textbook idiom for hopelessly insufficient help.

exercises.prompt: An alumnus donates a building and says "我只是___罷了." What did they say?
exercises.explanation: 飲水思源 — "drink water, remember its source." The standard humble phrase for a former student giving back.

exercises.prompt: A junior researcher publishes a quiet paper that quietly changes the field. Years later, a colleague says "她那篇論文真是 ___ — 之前大家幾乎都沒聽過她的名字." Fill the blank.
acceptableAnswers: 一鳴驚人 (yī míng jīng rén)
exercises.explanation: 一鳴驚人 — "one cry stuns everyone" — fits an unknown who astonishes. Standalone, without a near-synonym crowding it.

exercises.prompt: the higher-tier 成語 to its literal image

pairs.right: Crows and sparrows make no sound
A cup of water for a cartload of burning firewood

exercises.prompt: An editorial about a record-breaking heatwave opens with "今夏的高溫實屬___，氣象臺近百年來從未記錄過同等資料." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 前所未有 — "unprecedented" — fits records that break the historical baseline. Standard editorial collocation.

exercises.prompt: A judge enters the courtroom and the gallery instantly falls silent. A reporter writes "全場頓時___." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 鴉雀無聲 — even crows and sparrows are silent — is the textbook idiom for an instantly hushed crowd.

exercises.prompt: An award citation reads: "她獲此殊榮，可謂 ___ — 多年的耕耘終於得到了應有的認可." Pick the idiom that says "the reputation is earned."
acceptableAnswers: 名副其實 (míng fù qí shí)
exercises.explanation: 名副其實 — name matches reality — the standard endorsement of an earned title or reputation.

exercises.prompt: A tech blog warns: "創業者一夜爆紅的故事 ___，但持續輸出價值才是真正的難題." Pick the idiom signaling "unprecedented and stunning."
exercises.explanation: 一鳴驚人 here describes the splashy debut. The follow-up clause then deflates it — classic editorial rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Which of these would feel WRONG in an op-ed about fundraising falling short?
options: 募集到的款項不過 杯水車薪
募集到的款項實屬 鴉雀無聲
對受災群眾而言，杯水車薪也聊勝於無
面對龐大的缺口，這點錢無異於杯水車薪
exercises.answer: 募集到的款項實屬 鴉雀無聲
exercises.explanation: 鴉雀無聲 describes a silent crowd, not insufficient funds. A native reader would feel the misfit instantly. Distractor-spotting at C2 means recognizing the image inside each idiom.

exercises.answer: a cup of water on a burning cartload
exercises.explanation: 杯水 (a cup of water) + 車薪 (a cartload of burning firewood). The classic idiom of insufficiency.

exercises.prompt: An editorial closes: "對受災群眾而言，這點款項不過 ___." (4 characters) Fill the idiom of insufficiency.
exercises.explanation: 杯水車薪 — the standard editorial idiom for a grossly insufficient effort.

exercises.prompt: A famous unknown publishes a quiet but field-changing paper. The fitting idiom is:
exercises.explanation: 一鳴驚人 — "one cry stuns everyone." Fits an unknown who astonishes.

exercises.prompt: Build the editorial line: "Faced with such a huge gap, this sum is hardly more than a cup of water on a cartload of fire."
exercises.answer: 面對 龐大 的 缺口 這 點 錢 無 異 於 杯水車薪

exercises.prompt: the C2 idiom to a fitting context
An editorial intones a record-breaking idiom. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 今夏的高溫實屬前所未有
options: 今夏的高溫實屬前所未有
exercises.answer: 今夏的高溫實屬前所未有

acceptableAnswers: remember where the water came from
exercises.explanation: The humble alumnus's idiom.

exercises.prompt: A judge enters and the gallery hushes: "全場 頓時 ___." (4 characters)
exercises.explanation: 鴉雀無聲 — total silence in a crowd.

exercises.prompt: An award citation: "她獲 此 殊榮，可謂 ___ —— 多年 耕耘 終 得 認可." Pick the right idiom.
exercises.explanation: 名副其實 — "the title is earned" — endorses an earned reputation.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Her thesis truly amazed everyone — before that nearly no one had heard her name."
exercises.answer: 她 那 篇 論文 真是 一鳴驚人 之前 大家 幾乎 沒 聽 過 她 的 名字

lessons.title: 塞翁失馬 and the long forms
lessons.description: Idioms whose punchline is implied

exercises.prompt: "塞翁失馬" is short for "塞翁失馬，焉知非福." The full meaning is:
options: Bad luck now may prove to be good fortune later
A horse lost is a horse gone
The wise farmer never loses anything
exercises.answer: Bad luck now may prove to be good fortune later

exercises.prompt: Your friend missed a flight that later had a maintenance scare. Best response:
options: 看來是塞翁失馬 — talk about a blessing in disguise.
真是杯水車薪 — that hardly helps at all.
果然是名副其實 — the reputation is earned.
確實是鴉雀無聲 — you can hear a pin drop.
exercises.answer: 看來是塞翁失馬 — talk about a blessing in disguise.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Don't worry — this may turn out to be a blessing in disguise."
exercises.answer: 別 擔心 這 或許 是 塞翁失馬

exercises.prompt: the long-form idiom to the punchline that completes it
"百聞不如一見" is best paraphrased as:
options: Hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
It is better to hear than to see
A hundred questions deserve one answer
exercises.answer: Hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
exercises.explanation: The idiom is a stock argument for first-hand experience. Often quoted before someone visits a place they have only read about.

exercises.prompt: An interviewee says "我相信 三人行必有我師." The implied register is:
options: Confucian humility — there is always something to learn from others
A literal claim about three travelers
exercises.answer: Confucian humility — there is always something to learn from others
exercises.explanation: From 論語. Quoted to signal teachability without sounding self-deprecating.

exercises.prompt: After a startup pivot succeeds, the founder writes "當初被裁員，如今想來真是 ___ ， 焉知非福." Fill the missing four characters.
acceptableAnswers: 塞翁失馬 (sài wēng shī mǎ)
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失馬，焉知非福 — the long form. Setting the punchline behind the comma is a common rhetorical pattern.

exercises.prompt: Which scenario LEAST fits 塞翁失馬?
options: A canceled flight that avoids a maintenance issue
A failed job application that pushes someone into a better field
A chronic illness that forces healthier habits
A long-planned promotion that arrives on schedule
exercises.answer: A long-planned promotion that arrives on schedule
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失馬 requires an initial misfortune that turns out for the best. A smooth, on-time success is just success.

exercises.prompt: Build the long form: "Old man at the frontier loses his horse — how to know it isn't fortune?"
exercises.answer: 塞翁 失馬 焉 知 非 福

exercises.prompt: A professor quotes "學而不思則罔". The point being made is:
options: Learning without reflection leaves you confused / lost
Thinking is more important than learning
Both learning and thinking are useless
exercises.answer: Learning without reflection leaves you confused / lost
exercises.explanation: The full Analects line: 學而不思則罔，思而不學則殆 — both halves needed. 罔 here is closer to "lost / muddled" than "empty."

exercises.answer: an old man's lost horse — who knows it isn't a blessing
acceptableAnswers: bad luck may yet prove fortunate
the old man at the frontier lost his horse — perhaps a blessing
exercises.explanation: The classical long form. The punchline 焉知非福 carries the meaning.

exercises.prompt: After a startup pivot saved by the layoff: "當 初 被 裁 員，如今 想來 真 是 ___ ， 焉 知 非 福." (4 characters)
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失馬 — set up; 焉知非福 — punchline.

exercises.prompt: An interviewee says "三人行 必有 我師" — what register and what attitude?
options: Confucian humility — there's always something to learn
A literal claim about three travelers
exercises.answer: Confucian humility — there's always something to learn
exercises.explanation: From 論語. Quoted to signal teachability.

exercises.prompt: Build the long form: "Old man at the frontier lost his horse — how to know it isn't fortune?"
exercises.answer: 塞翁 失馬 焉 知 非 福

exercises.prompt: the long-form opening to its punchline
A friend offers a long-form consolation. Pick what you hear.
options: 塞翁丟馬，怎麼知道不是好事
丟了馬的老頭，可能是福氣

exercises.answer: hearing a hundred times is not as good as seeing once
acceptableAnswers: one look beats a hundred reports
exercises.explanation: The stock argument for first-hand experience.

exercises.prompt: Confucian classic: "學 而 不 思 則 ___." (one character)
exercises.explanation: 學而不思則罔 — learning without reflection leaves one lost.

exercises.prompt: Which scenario LEAST fits 塞翁失馬?
options: A canceled flight that avoided a maintenance scare
A failed job application that pushed someone into a better field
A chronic illness that forced healthier habits
A long-planned promotion that arrived on schedule
exercises.answer: A long-planned promotion that arrived on schedule
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失馬 needs an initial misfortune that turns out for the best.

exercises.prompt: Build the Analects line: "Learning without reflection leaves one lost; reflection without learning is perilous."
exercises.answer: 學 而 不 思 則 罔 思 而 不 學 則 殆

lessons.title: 歇後語 — set-up and punchline
lessons.description: The two-part sayings every native speaker recognizes

exercises.prompt: the set-up to the punchline
我現在真是泥菩薩過江啊…
exercises.hint: A coworker says this — what do they mean?
options: I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.answer: I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.explanation: The implied 自身難保 — "can't even save myself." A polite way to refuse a favor.

exercises.prompt: You worked on a project for a year and the client cancels. A friend says "哎，真是竹籃打水…" What's implied?
options: All your effort came to nothing (一場空)
exercises.answer: All your effort came to nothing (一場空)

exercises.prompt: Project manager says: "這次大家就 ___, 各顯神通吧!" Fill in the set-up.
exercises.explanation: 八仙過海，各顯神通 — each team member should bring their own special skills.

exercises.prompt: the 歇後語 set-up to the implied meaning in plain Mandarin
"竹籃打水，一場空" — which English captures the rhythm best?
options: Drawing water with a bamboo basket — all for nothing
A basket of bamboo — empty in shape only
Pouring water into bamboo — the drink keeps coming
exercises.answer: Drawing water with a bamboo basket — all for nothing
exercises.explanation: The two-part structure: image (basket can't hold water) → moral (effort came to nothing). The translation has to keep both halves visible.

exercises.prompt: Two coworkers are stretched thin and a third asks for help. One whispers: "我現在真是 ___ 過江，自身難保啊." Fill in the blanks.
exercises.explanation: 泥菩薩過江，自身難保 — a clay Bodhisattva crossing a river can't even save itself. The standard polite refusal.

exercises.prompt: Which 歇後語 best fits this situation: a junior employee endures unfair blame at a meeting and can't push back without losing their job.
options: 啞巴吃黃連，有苦說不出
exercises.answer: 啞巴吃黃連，有苦說不出
exercises.explanation: Bitterness that can't be voiced — exactly the office-grievance scenario.

exercises.prompt: 歇後語 are most natural in which register?
options: Casual speech, online chat, family conversation
exercises.answer: Casual speech, online chat, family conversation
exercises.explanation: 歇後語 are colloquial — they bring warmth and humor. Avoid them in formal print; reach for 成語 instead.

exercises.prompt: Build the full saying: "Eight Immortals crossing the sea — each shows their own divine skill."
exercises.answer: 八仙 過海 各 顯 神通
the Eight Immortals cross the sea, each showing their divine skill
exercises.explanation: The team-ad-lib 歇後語.

exercises.prompt: Project manager says: "這次 大家 就 ___ ，各 顯 神 通 吧." (4 characters)
exercises.explanation: 八仙過海，各顯神通 — "each plays their strength."

exercises.prompt: A coworker says "我現在真是 泥菩薩過江啊." What's implied?
options: I am extremely busy and successful
I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.answer: I can't help you — I'm in trouble myself
exercises.explanation: Implied 自身難保 — clay Bodhisattva can't even save itself.

exercises.prompt: Build the saying: "A clay Bodhisattva crossing the river — even itself it cannot save."
exercises.answer: 泥菩薩 過 江 自身 難 保

exercises.prompt: the 歇後語 to its plain-Mandarin punchline
A friend sighs about a failed venture. Pick what you hear.

exercises.answer: drawing water with a bamboo basket — all for nothing
acceptableAnswers: bamboo basket for water — empty result
exercises.explanation: Two-part 歇後語. Image + moral.

exercises.prompt: Polite refusal: "我 現 在 真是 泥 菩 薩 過 江，自 身 ___ 保 啊." (one character)
exercises.explanation: 自身難保 — can't even save oneself.

exercises.prompt: 歇後語 are most natural in which register?
options: Casual speech, online chat, family conversation
exercises.answer: Casual speech, online chat, family conversation
exercises.explanation: 歇後語 are colloquial — warm, vivid. Formal print prefers 成語.

exercises.prompt: Build the saying: "Drawing water with a bamboo basket — all for nothing."
exercises.answer: 竹籃 打 水 一 場 空

lessons.title: Suffering you can't voice
lessons.description: 啞巴吃黃連 and the idioms of swallowed pain

exercises.prompt: 我真是啞巴吃黃連…
exercises.hint: An employee who can't complain about an unfair boss says this — what does it mean?
options: I have bitterness I can't speak of
exercises.answer: I have bitterness I can't speak of
exercises.explanation: 黃連 is a bitter Chinese herb. Implied second half: 有苦說不出.

exercises.prompt: the saying to a situation it fits

pairs.right: Deal collapses after months of work
Refusing a favor when you're stretched thin
Team ad-libs — each plays their strength

exercises.prompt: Which is more likely in a formal newspaper editorial?
exercises.explanation: 成語 (four-character, classical) belong in editorials. 歇後語 are colloquial and rare in formal print.

exercises.prompt: 黃連 in 啞巴吃黃連 refers to:
exercises.explanation: 黃連 is one of the bitterest items in the traditional pharmacy. The image: someone unable to speak but with the worst taste in their mouth.

exercises.prompt: Complete the saying: "啞巴吃黃連，有 ___ 說不出."
exercises.explanation: 苦 here is doing double duty — literal bitterness (the herb) and metaphorical suffering (the unspoken grievance).

exercises.prompt: A novelist wants to describe a daughter-in-law trapped in an unfair household, suffering quietly for years. The most fitting phrase:
options: 她真是啞巴吃黃連，有苦說不出

topics.title: Confucian and Daoist concepts
topics.description: 仁、義、道、無為 — the philosophical vocabulary in modern usage

guide.intro: Modern Mandarin is haunted by two-and-a-half-thousand-year-old conversations. Words like 仁 (rén), 義 (yì), 道 (dào), and 無為 (wú wéi) appear in HR slogans, parenting books, and political speeches — usually drained of their original technical force, but never entirely. To read Chinese deeply you have to feel the philosophical residue.

sections.text: Confucian core: 仁 and 義

仁 (rén) is humaneness — the disposition to treat others as fully human. 義 (yì) is righteousness — doing the right thing even at cost. The compound 仁義 is shorthand for moral character. When a CEO is praised as 有仁義 (yǒu rén yì), they are being called principled, not merely successful.

rows.source: 他 是 一 個 仁義 之 人。
rows.pinyin: Tā shì yí gè rényì zhī rén.
rows.translation: He is a man of humaneness and integrity.

rows.source: 見 利 忘 義
rows.translation: See profit and forget righteousness — chase money and ditch principle.
Give up life to grasp righteousness — die for principle.

sections.text: 禮 — propriety, ritual, manners

禮 (lǐ) is the choreography of how relationships should be enacted — bowing depths, gift weights, who eats first. In modern business, 禮 survives as 禮貌 (politeness), 禮物 (gift), 送禮 (gift-giving), and the everyday verb 失禮 (to be rude / lose face by a breach of manners).

rows.source: 禮 多 人 不 怪
rows.translation: Excessive courtesy is never resented.

rows.source: 來 而 不 往 非 禮 也
rows.pinyin: Lái ér bù wǎng fēi lǐ yě
rows.translation: To receive and not give back is not 禮 — i.e. you must reciprocate.

sections.text: Daoist counterweight: 道 and 無為

道 (dào) is the underlying way of things — natural, ungraspable. 無為 (wú wéi) is "non-coercive action" — accomplishing through alignment rather than force. Modern usage has softened both: 道理 (reason, principle), 知道 (literally "know the way" — the everyday "to know"), 無為而治 (governing by stepping back).

rows.translation: Follow its natural course — let things be.
Govern by non-action — manage by enabling, not directing.
The highest good is like water — yielding, low-seeking, ultimately unstoppable.

sections.text: 上善若水 from the 道德經 is engraved on countless tea-shop walls and tech-CEO LinkedIn bios. Recognize it as Daoist signaling — humility-by-quotation.
中庸 — the middle way

中庸 (zhōng yōng), "the doctrine of the mean," prizes balance over extremes. In modern business and family advice, 中庸之道 (zhōng yōng zhī dào) is the polite phrase for "don't overdo it either way." Speakers reaching for it want to sound measured, even-keeled, philosophically grounded.

rows.source: 我 主張 走 中庸 之 道。
rows.pinyin: Wǒ zhǔzhāng zǒu zhōngyōng zhī dào.
rows.translation: I advocate the middle way.

sections.text: Be careful: 中庸 in younger urban use can be subtly negative — "wishy-washy, refuses to take a side." Read the speaker's tone.

topics.title: Regional language awareness
topics.description: Mainland Putonghua, Taiwan Guoyu, and the Cantonese world

guide.intro: "Chinese" is several languages and several standardizations of one. C2 means you can hear someone speak for ten seconds and tell whether they grew up in Beijing, Taipei, Guangzhou, or Singapore — and adjust your own usage accordingly. You won't speak every variant. You will learn to recognize and respect them.

sections.text: Putonghua vs Guoyu — same language, different standard

Mainland 普通話 (pǔtōnghuà) and Taiwan 國語 (guóyǔ) are the same language with different standardizations: simplified vs traditional characters, mainland Pinyin vs Taiwanese Zhuyin (注音), distinct vocabulary for many modern objects.
On the mainland 土豆 = potato. In Taiwan 土豆 = peanut. This single word has caused decades of dinner-party confusion.
Tone and accent cues

Mainland Putonghua, especially Beijing-flavored, has heavy 兒化音 (érhuàyīn, the rhotic suffix) — 哪兒、玩兒、有點兒. Taiwan Guoyu generally drops 兒化, prefers softer tones, and sounds the neutral tone less aggressively. Southern mainland speakers (Shanghai, Guangzhou) often blur the n/l distinction or merge zh/z, ch/c, sh/s.

rows.translation: Where are you? — Beijing-flavored.
Where are you? — Taiwan / southern / formal.

sections.text: Cantonese — a separate Chinese language

廣東話 / 粵語 (Cantonese) is mutually unintelligible with Mandarin in speech, though written Standard Chinese is shared. Cantonese has six tones (some count nine), retains classical Chinese consonant clusters lost in Mandarin, and uses distinct vocabulary: 唔 (m̀h, not) for 不, 佢 (kéuih) for 他, 食 (sihk) for 吃.

rows.translation: Have you eaten? — Cantonese, written informally.

rows.source: 你 吃 了 飯 沒有？
rows.pinyin: Nǐ chī le fàn méi yǒu? (Mandarin)
rows.translation: Same question, Mandarin.

sections.text: When you see characters like 嘅、咗、嗮、咩、嘢 in writing — that's written Cantonese (粵文), common on Hong Kong social media but unusual in mainland publications.
Singapore, Malaysia, overseas

Singaporean Mandarin (新加坡華語) is heavily code-mixed with English, Hokkien, and Malay. Vocabulary like 巴剎 (bāshā, market — from Malay pasar) and 德士 (déshì, taxi — from English) is locally standard but invisible on the mainland. Malaysian Chinese communities use similar mixes. Overseas Chinese in the US/Australia often retain pre-1949 vocabulary — 老中 for "older Chinese folks," or older transliterations.
Cross-strait political vocabulary — read the labels

Political register is where word choice tells you the speaker's stance. 大陸 (dàlù, "the mainland") and 內地 (nèidì, "the interior") describe the same territory but signal different framings — 內地 is the term Hong Kong and Macau use within the One-Country framework; Taiwan media usually prefer 中國大陸 or simply 中國. Likewise, 政府 (zhèngfǔ) is neutral "government," while 當局 (dāngjú, "the authorities") is more distanced — used by foreign-press translations and by speakers who want a faintly skeptical tone.

rows: Taiwan media, Hong Kong, overseas Chinese
"The interior" — frames PRC as the inside

sections.text: These choices are not interchangeable. Calling Taiwan's elected government 臺灣當局 ("the Taiwan authorities") rather than 臺灣政府 is itself a political signal — standard in PRC official media. Reading register includes reading these tells.

exercises.prompt: "我去巴剎買菜。" Where is the speaker most likely from?
exercises.explanation: 巴剎 (bāshā) is from Malay pasar (market). Locally standard in Singapore/Malaysia, almost never heard on the mainland.

exercises.explanation: From English "taxi." Mainland equivalent: 計程車. Taiwan: 計程車.

exercises.prompt: Mainland Mandarin uses 影片 for video; Taiwan uses ___.
An article writes "臺灣當局" rather than "臺灣政府". This word choice signals:
options: A PRC-aligned framing — distancing the elected government as "the authorities"
An academic term with no political weight
exercises.answer: A PRC-aligned framing — distancing the elected government as "the authorities"
exercises.explanation: 當局 ("the authorities") refuses the term 政府 ("government"). In cross-strait writing it is a standard PRC-state-media tell. Reading register means catching this.

exercises.prompt: A Hong Kong government press release uses "內地" while a Taiwan newspaper uses "中國大陸" for the same territory. Why?
options: Same referent, different framings — 內地 fits a One-Country frame; 中國大陸 keeps explicit distance
They refer to different time periods
exercises.answer: Same referent, different framings — 內地 fits a One-Country frame; 中國大陸 keeps explicit distance
exercises.explanation: Same place, different rhetorical relationship. 內地 ("the interior") presupposes you're inside the same country; 中國大陸 names it as a separate political entity.

exercises.prompt: the cross-strait term to the framing it carries

exercises.explanation: Diaspora-flavored shorthand for 老一輩中國人. Almost never appears in mainland or Taiwan press; common in US/Australia Chinese papers.

exercises.prompt: Singapore Mandarin is most distinctive for:

exercises.answer: Code-mixing with English, Hokkien, and Malay
exercises.explanation: Singapore Mandarin sits inside a multilingual ecology; loanwords like 巴剎 (Malay) and 德士 (English) are locally standard, not slang.

exercises.prompt: A Beijing news anchor refers to Taipei's elected government as "臺灣 ___ " rather than "臺灣政府". Fill in the politically loaded term.
exercises.explanation: 臺灣當局 is the standard PRC state-media phrasing. The substitution refuses the term 政府 — a small but consistent rhetorical signal.

topics.title: Media literacy and register
topics.description: Reading newspapers, recognizing propaganda, parsing satire

guide.intro: Reading Chinese news is not just decoding characters — it's reading register. The same event in 人民日報, 財新, BBC中文, 華爾街日報 中文版, and a 微博 satire account will appear in five distinct linguistic costumes. C2 means recognizing the costume.

sections.text: Boilerplate of the official register

Official Chinese reporting has a recognizable lexicon. When you see clusters of the phrases below, you are reading 黨媒 (party media) or material that closely echoes it. They are not necessarily false — they are signals of register and stance.

rows: "The relevant authorities" — bureaucratic vagueness, agent unspecified
bù kě gào rén de mùdì
"Ulterior motives" — strong accusation of bad faith
"Hurt the feelings of the X people" — diplomatic outrage marker
"Seek progress while maintaining stability" — economic policy slogan

sections.text: "傷害中國人民的感情" is so formulaic that it has become a Chinese-internet joke. Recognizing the joke is part of recognizing the register.
Hedges of independent reporting

Independent or commercial Chinese-language reporting (財新, 端傳媒, 聯合早報, BBC中文) tends to use sourced hedges absent from official copy: 據悉, 據知情人士透露, 多名…表示, 截至發稿. These are signals of journalistic register.

rows.pinyin: jù zhī qíng rén shì tòu lù
rows.translation: According to sources familiar with the matter — Wall Street Journal cliché translated wholesale into Chinese.
At the time of publication — used to flag information that might change.
Has not yet responded — neutral phrasing for a no-comment situation.

sections.text: Satire and irony online

Chinese internet culture is famously inventive about evading censorship and signaling irony. Watch for: deliberate typos and homophones ("河蟹" hé xiè, "river crab", for the censored 和諧 héxié, "harmony"); reversed praise ("厲害了，我的國" — originally earnest, often deployed sarcastically now); the bracket-and-comma sneer like 「（笑）」 or 233333 (laughter); and the soft "emmm…" hedge marking polite disagreement.

rows.translation: "Awesome, my country" + "(laughs)" — sarcasm.

rows.pinyin: Zhè bō cāozuò wǒ gěi mǎn fēn
rows.translation: I give this move a perfect ten — almost always sarcastic praise of a misstep.
Those who understand, understand — wink, the censored thing.

sections.text: "懂的都懂" is a strong tell. The writer is naming the unspoken topic without naming it; you're being included in an in-group of readers.
Headline conventions

Chinese-language headlines compress aggressively. Expect colons, slashes, and bracketed labels: 【獨家】 (exclusive), 【深度】 (deep dive), 【快訊】 (breaking). The colon often introduces the subject's quote: 張三：我沒說過那句話.

exercises.prompt: the boilerplate phrase to its function

"傷害中國人民的感情" is recognized by Chinese readers as:

exercises.explanation: Official register cluster: 我方 (formal first person), 表示強烈不滿 (formulaic outrage), 有關方面 (vague agent), 嚴正交涉 (diplomatic-protest cliché).

exercises.answer: Lower — concern voiced but the door is left open
exercises.explanation: These phrases form a graduated scale. 嚴重關切 is at the lower end; 強烈譴責 and 保留採取必要措施 are escalations. Reading the scale matters.

exercises.prompt: A press release reads: "任何企圖傷害中國人民感情的行徑，必將遭到全體中國人民的堅決反對." The piece is best characterized as:

exercises.prompt: "有關部門" ("the relevant authorities") works rhetorically because:

It names no specific agency — preserving bureaucratic ambiguity
It refers only to local government
exercises.answer: It names no specific agency — preserving bureaucratic ambiguity
exercises.explanation: The phrase is a bureaucratic shield. It assigns responsibility without identifying anyone. Recognizing this evasion is part of media literacy.

lessons.title: Hedges of independent reporting
lessons.description: 據悉, 截至發稿, 尚無回應

exercises.prompt: the journalistic hedge to its sense

pairs.right: It is reported / it is understood

exercises.prompt: A reporter writes "截至發稿，該公司尚無回應." This signals:
options: The company refused to comment angrily
The reporter hadn't received a response by deadline; the situation may evolve
exercises.answer: The reporter hadn't received a response by deadline; the situation may evolve

lessons.description: 河蟹, 233, and "懂的都懂"

exercises.prompt: 我的帖子被河蟹了
exercises.hint: What does this internet-slang phrase most likely mean?
exercises.explanation: 河蟹 (river crab) is a homophone for 和諧 (harmony), the official slogan around content control. The substitution turns censorship into a joke.

exercises.prompt: 懂的都懂
exercises.hint: A comment thread ends with this — what is its function?
options: A literal claim that the topic is easy
A wink at a censored or sensitive subject — "you know what I mean"
A request to explain in detail
exercises.answer: A wink at a censored or sensitive subject — "you know what I mean"

exercises.prompt: "這波操作我給滿分" written under a video of a clearly bad mistake is:
On Chinese social media, what does the number "233" signify?
exercises.explanation: From an old BBS emoji #233 (a laughing face). The string "23333…" is the Chinese-internet equivalent of "lololol."

exercises.prompt: the internet-satire device to its decoded meaning
A microblog post about a banned topic ends with "emmm…". This particle is doing what?
exercises.explanation: The hedged "emmm…" — borrowed from English — softens criticism, especially around politically risky topics.

exercises.prompt: A meme reads "等等黨永遠滴神" about consumers who wait for product price drops. The register is:
exercises.explanation: 永遠滴神 ("forever the god," written with 滴 instead of 的 for meme effect) is exaggerated playful praise. 等等黨 names the social tribe of "wait-and-see" buyers. Pure online register.

exercises.prompt: A Weibo post says "我的帖子又被 ___ 蟹了." Fill in the missing character (the homophone-pun substitute for 和).
exercises.explanation: 河蟹 (river crab) is the homophone-evading substitute for 和諧 (harmony / harmonize / censor). The pun lets writers name censorship without naming it.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence is most likely INTENDED sincerely rather than sarcastically?
options: 在醫護人員的努力下，疫情得到了有效控制。
exercises.answer: 在醫護人員的努力下，疫情得到了有效控制。
exercises.explanation: Bracketed laughter, sarcasm tells, and 懂的都懂 are all irony markers. The medical-effort sentence has no irony cue and reads as straight reporting.

exercises.prompt: Why did Chinese netizens originally adopt homophone substitutions like 河蟹 and 草泥馬?
options: To evade automated censorship of the original characters
exercises.answer: To evade automated censorship of the original characters
exercises.explanation: Filter-evasion is the structural origin. Once the homophones spread, they became cultural in-jokes in their own right — the censorship is the punchline.

exercises.explanation: 評論 = opinion / commentary. Readers know to read for argument, not for facts.

topics.title: Formal essay structure (論說文)
topics.description: Openings, transitions, conclusions — the conventions of academic Chinese argument

guide.intro: 議論文 (yìlùnwén) — the argumentative essay — is the dominant academic genre in Chinese high schools, university entrance exams, and editorial pages. It has its own conventions: sourced openings, signposted transitions, weighty conclusions. C2 essay writing means writing inside this scaffold rather than translating English structure into Chinese words.

sections.text: The opening (開篇 kāipiān)

A 議論文 typically opens with one of three moves: a quoted line of classical or canonical authority (借古立論), an observation of a current phenomenon (現象切入), or a counter-position that the writer will then refute (破題). All three are register-marked — the colloquial "let me tell you about a friend of mine…" opener that works in English would feel out of place.

rows.source: 古人云："讀萬卷書，行萬里路." 此言至今仍有 深意。
rows.pinyin: Gǔrén yún: dú wàn juàn shū, xíng wàn lǐ lù. Cǐ yán zhì jīn réng yǒu shēnyì.
rows.translation: The ancients said: "Read ten thousand books, walk ten thousand li." These words still carry deep meaning today.

rows.source: 近年來，人工智慧 之 發展 日新月異。
rows.pinyin: Jìnnián lái, réngōng zhìnéng zhī fāzhǎn rìxīnyuèyì.
rows.translation: In recent years, the development of AI has changed by the day. (Phenomenon opener.)

sections.text: Transitions (過渡 guòdù)

Chinese academic writing signals its structure overtly. Each new paragraph typically begins with a connector that names its function: 首先 (first), 其次 (next), 再者 (furthermore), 此外 (besides this), 然而 (however), 反觀 (looking conversely at), 綜上所述 (summing up the above). Skip these and the essay reads as choppy, no matter how strong each paragraph is on its own.

rows: 首先 / 其次 / 再者
From this we can see — drawing inference
In sum / from all the above — pre-conclusion marker

sections.text: The body argument

Each body paragraph typically follows a 論點-論據-論證 structure: state a thesis-claim (論點), give evidence (論據), explain the reasoning (論證). The evidence is often a citation of a 名人 ("famous figure"), a historical episode, or a contemporary statistic. Hedges like 據統計, 研究表明, 不可否認 and 必須承認 mark the move from claim to evidence.

rows.source: 據統計，超過 七成 的 受訪者 表示 …
rows.pinyin: Jù tǒngjì, chāoguò qī chéng de shòufǎngzhě biǎoshì…
rows.translation: Statistics show that over 70 percent of respondents say…

rows.source: 不可否認，問題 之 複雜 遠 超 預期。
rows.pinyin: Bù kě fǒurèn, wèntí zhī fùzá yuǎn chāo yùqī.
rows.translation: It cannot be denied that the problem is far more complex than expected.

sections.text: The conclusion (結尾 jiéwěi)

The conclusion is rarely a meek English-style "in conclusion, …". A strong 議論文 ending circles back to the opening (照應開頭), restates the thesis with elevated weight, and often closes with a four-character flourish or a forward-looking call. The phrases 綜上所述, 由此可見, 總而言之 cue the reader to expect the wrap-up.

rows.source: 綜上所述，唯有 持之以恆，方 能 致遠。
rows.pinyin: Zōng shàng suǒ shù, wéi yǒu chí zhī yǐ héng, fāng néng zhì yuǎn.
rows.translation: In sum: only with perseverance can one reach far. ("方能" is the elevated form of 才能.)

sections.text: Convention #1 of academic Chinese: prefer the 4-character cadence in your closing line. 持之以恆, 方能致遠, 任重道遠, 砥礪前行 — these are not clichés, they are tonal closers that signal the essay is ending with weight.

lessons.title: Openings of the academic essay
lessons.description: 古人云, 現象切入, and the 破題 move

exercises.prompt: An essay opens with "古人云：\"讀萬卷書，行萬里路.\"" This is which type of opening?
exercises.explanation: 古人云 / 古語有云 / 子曰 — all are signals that the writer is opening with a citation of canonical authority before staking their own thesis.

exercises.prompt: the opening type to its function
Build a phenomenon-opener: "In recent years, the development of AI has changed by the day."
exercises.answer: 近年來 人工智慧 之 發展 日新月異

exercises.prompt: An essay opens "有人 認為 教育 應當 以 應試 為 重 ， 然而 …". This is which opening type?
options: Refutation (破題) — set up the opposing view to demolish
exercises.answer: Refutation (破題) — set up the opposing view to demolish
exercises.explanation: 有人認為…然而… is the classic 破題 frame — name the position you'll refute, then pivot. Beloved by 議論文 writers.

exercises.prompt: Build a quoted-authority opener: "Confucius said: 'Learning without thinking leads to confusion.' These words still hold today."
exercises.answer: 子 曰 學 而 不 思 則 罔 此 言 至今 仍 不 過時

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads an opening line in essay register. Pick what you hear.

options: 古人云讀萬卷書行萬里路，此言至今仍有深意
古人說要多讀書多走路，到現在還是有道理
據說古代的人喜歡讀書旅行，今天看來也不錯
我覺得讀書和旅行都很重要
exercises.answer: 古人云讀萬卷書行萬里路，此言至今仍有深意
exercises.explanation: 古人云 + classical 4-4 quotation + 此言 + 至今仍 — full essay-register stack. The distractors paraphrase in conversational, semi-formal, or first-person registers.

exercises.prompt: An essay opens with "___ 雲 ， '己所不欲 ， 勿施於人.'" Fill the canonical attribution-frame (2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 古人云 / 古語有云 — both are formulaic openers attributing a saying to canonical antiquity. Standard 議論文 move.

exercises.prompt: the opening template to the rhetorical move it announces

lessons.title: Transitions and signposting
lessons.description: 首先 / 其次 / 再者 / 反觀 — making structure visible

exercises.prompt: the transition to its function
Halfway through an essay, a paragraph begins with "反觀西方教育體系…". The writer is signaling:
options: A summary of what was just said
A pivot to a contrasting case used as comparison
exercises.answer: A pivot to a contrasting case used as comparison
exercises.explanation: 反觀 = "by contrast / looking conversely at." A standard structural move in 議論文 — pivot to the comparison case to sharpen the thesis.

exercises.prompt: The pre-conclusion marker that means "summing up the above" is ___ (4 characters).
acceptableAnswers: 綜上所述 (zōng shàng suǒ shù)
exercises.explanation: 綜上所述 cues the reader: the wrap-up paragraph is starting. A near-mandatory move in formal Chinese essays.

exercises.prompt: An essay paragraph begins "不僅如此 ， 此 現象 在 農村 地區 尤為 明顯." The 不僅如此 signals:
options: A new topic unrelated to the previous
exercises.explanation: 不僅如此 = "not only this" — a paragraph-level escalation that adds weight to the prior point. Standard essay rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Build a transition-rich sentence: "From this we can see that education reform must consider both efficiency and fairness."
exercises.answer: 由此 可見 教育 改革 必須 兼顧 效率 與 公平

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions of a transition sentence. Pick the most essay-formal one.
exercises.spokenText: 綜上所述，唯有兼顧效率與公平，方能行穩致遠
options: 綜上所述，唯有兼顧效率與公平，方能行穩致遠
總的來說，只有同時考慮效率和公平，才能走得遠
總而言之，效率和公平都要兼顧，才能走得穩
我覺得，效率和公平都重要，這樣才能長久
exercises.answer: 綜上所述，唯有兼顧效率與公平，方能行穩致遠
exercises.explanation: 綜上所述 (formal pre-conclusion) + 唯有 (literary "only") + 方能 (literary 才能) + 4-character closer 行穩致遠. Full essay register. The distractors are progressively more colloquial.

exercises.prompt: each paragraph-opening transition to its position in an essay
An essay pivots: "反觀 ___ 教育 體系，注重 學生 的 自主 探索." Fill the standard contrastive territory (2 characters; opposite of 中國).
exercises.explanation: 反觀西方教育體系… is the canonical pivot in Chinese essays comparing systems. 反觀 + the contrastive case is a structural workhorse.

exercises.explanation: 由此可見 = "from this we can see" — the writer is drawing a conclusion from preceding evidence. The phrase is a pivot from data to claim.

lessons.title: Evidence and argument hedges
lessons.description: 據統計 / 研究表明 / 不可否認 / 必須承認

exercises.prompt: the hedge to its move in the argument
An essay paragraph reads: "不可否認，問題之複雜遠超預期。然而…". The 不可否認…然而… pair functions as:
options: Concession then pivot — "granted X, but Y"
A direct contradiction with no resolution
exercises.answer: Concession then pivot — "granted X, but Y"
exercises.explanation: 不可否認 lets you grant the opposing view's strongest point; 然而 then pivots to your counter-argument. Standard rhetorical move in formal argument.

exercises.prompt: Build: "Statistics show that over 70 percent of respondents are dissatisfied with this policy."
exercises.answer: 據統計 超過 七成 的 受訪者 對 此 政策 不 滿意

exercises.prompt: Which hedge would you use to introduce a peer-reviewed academic finding?
exercises.explanation: 研究表明 = "research shows / studies indicate" — the formal citation hedge for scholarly findings. 據統計 cites numbers; 聽說 / 好像 are conversational and out of register.

exercises.prompt: Build a long concession-pivot sentence: "It must be admitted that the new technology brings convenience; nevertheless, the privacy risks cannot be ignored."
exercises.answer: 必須 承認 新 技術 帶來 便利 然而 隱私 風險 不 容 忽視

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads a citation-hedged claim. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 研究表明，長期睡眠不足將顯著提高心血管疾病的風險
options: 研究表明，長期睡眠不足將顯著提高心血管疾病的風險
聽說睡得少不好，對心臟不太好
據說睡眠不足會讓人得心血管病
exercises.answer: 研究表明，長期睡眠不足將顯著提高心血管疾病的風險
exercises.explanation: 研究表明 + 顯著提高 + 心血管疾病 — academic-register stack with quantified verb and technical noun phrase. The distractors are colloquial.

exercises.prompt: the hedge to what it actually concedes

pairs.right: Conceding the opposing view's strongest point
Acknowledging an unavoidable counter — "one must admit"

exercises.prompt: An essay sets up a concession: "___ 否認，問題 之 複雜 遠 超 預期 ， 然而 …". Fill the literary 3-character hedge.
exercises.explanation: 不可否認 = "it cannot be denied" — the formal concession that lets you grant the strongest opposing point before pivoting with 然而.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence shows the cleanest 論點-論據-論證 (claim-evidence-reasoning) structure?
options: 教育 是 好 東西 — 我 覺得

我 喜歡 學習 ， 我 同學 也 喜歡
學習 重要 — 大家 都 知道
exercises.answer: 教育 改變 人生 ， 據 統計 ， 受 高等教育 者 收入 平均 高 出 三 成 ， 因此 政策 應 予 支援
exercises.explanation: Three moves: 論點 (claim — education changes lives), 論據 (evidence — statistics on income), 論證 (reasoning — therefore support the policy). The other options stop at claim or assertion only.

lessons.title: Conclusions with weight
lessons.description: 綜上所述, 4-character closers, and 方能 elevation

exercises.prompt: 唯有持之以恆，方能致遠。
exercises.hint: What is 方能 the elevated form of?
exercises.explanation: 方能 (fāng néng) is the literary register of 才能 — "only then can." Standard in formal essay closers.

exercises.prompt: the 4-character closer to its sense

pairs.right: The burden is heavy and the road long

exercises.prompt: Build a weighty conclusion: "In sum, only with perseverance can one reach far."
exercises.answer: 綜上所述 唯有 持之以恆 方能 致遠

exercises.prompt: Why do Chinese academic essays often close with a 4-character idiom?
options: It is a tonal convention — the cadence signals the essay is ending with weight
exercises.answer: It is a tonal convention — the cadence signals the essay is ending with weight
exercises.explanation: Convention, not decoration. A C2-fluent essay rounds out with 4-character cadence the same way an English essay might land on a parallel triplet.

exercises.prompt: Build a weighty multi-clause closer: "In sum, the road ahead is long and the burden heavy; only by forging ahead together can we reach far."
exercises.answer: 綜上所述 任重 而 道遠 唯有 砥礪 前行 方能 致遠

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions of an essay closer. Pick the one with the proper essay-register weight.
exercises.spokenText: 綜上所述，唯有持之以恆，方能致遠
options: 綜上所述，唯有持之以恆，方能致遠
總的來說，只有堅持下去才能走得遠
總而言之，要堅持不懈，才能成功
我覺得只要堅持就一定能成功
exercises.answer: 綜上所述，唯有持之以恆，方能致遠
exercises.explanation: 綜上所述 + 唯有 + 4-character idiom 持之以恆 + 方能致遠 — quadruple essay-register stack. The distractors progressively descend toward conversational register.

exercises.prompt: Complete the closer: "___ 可見 ， 教育 改革 任重道遠 ， ___ 砥礪 前行 ， 方能 行穩致遠." Fill the inference marker (2 characters) and the precondition marker (2 characters).
exercises.explanation: 由此 ("from this") + 可見 forms the inference move; 唯有 ("only by") + 4-character verb phrase forms the precondition for the 4-character payoff. Standard essay closer skeleton.

exercises.prompt: Which 4-character closer best fits an essay arguing that reform must be sustained over decades?
exercises.explanation: 持之以恆 = "persevere over the long run" — the canonical closer for any essay arguing for sustained effort. The other three idioms describe silence, gratitude, and reversed fortune respectively.

exercises.prompt: Build an inference-pre-conclusion bridge: "From the above analysis, we can see that only when system, education, and culture work together can we move forward steadily and reach far."

topics.title: C2 review — register, idiom, classical, rhythm
topics.description: Mixed-register paragraph parsing, idiom-in-context, register identification, and parallel rewriting

guide.intro: C2 mastery is not knowing one register — it's switching between them in a paragraph and recognizing the switch when someone else does it. This review pulls together classical particles, 成語 in modern context, register identification, and the rhythm of parallel construction.

sections.text: What this review tests

Four lessons, each targeting one C2-level skill: (1) parsing paragraphs that mix classical particles with modern register; (2) identifying which 成語 fits a real headline / news context out of multiple plausible candidates; (3) reading a paragraph and naming its register (official, independent press, satire, literary, academic); (4) recognizing imbalanced parallel constructions and rewriting them so the rhythm holds.
If a question feels like it has two right answers, it usually does — at C2 the test is often "which is more idiomatic / more in-register," not "which is grammatical."

lessons.title: Mixed-register paragraph parsing
lessons.description: Classical particles in modern prose — read, then identify the function

exercises.prompt: A 財新 editorial reads: "眾所周知，此次改革之於國民經濟，影響深遠。然而，其執行之難，前所未有。" Which classical particle is doing the most structural work?
options: 之 — modifier-linker (here connecting nouns into formal phrases)
exercises.answer: 之 — modifier-linker (here connecting nouns into formal phrases)
exercises.explanation: 之於 (relation to), 改革之… (this reform's…), 其執行之難 (the difficulty of its execution). Three uses of 之 carry the editorial register.

exercises.prompt: each phrase from the editorial above to its function

pairs.left: 此次改革之於國民經濟
pairs.right: 之於 — X's relation to Y

exercises.prompt: A government report uses "是以本部門決定…". The 是以 is functioning as:
Build a mixed-register sentence: "The reasons are three; this we cannot ignore."
exercises.answer: 其 原因 有 三 此 不可 忽視

exercises.prompt: An editorial writes "此 乃 國 之 大 事 也." The sentence-final 也 functions as:
exercises.explanation: Sentence-final classical 也 was an assertion-marker in literary Chinese (≈ "… is the case"). Here it pairs with 此乃 + 之 to mark elevated register. The modern "also" 也 occupies a totally different syntactic slot.

exercises.prompt: Build a long mixed-register editorial sentence: "The development of artificial intelligence is the great trend of our time; it cannot be reversed, nor should it be feared."
exercises.answer: 人工智慧 之 發展 乃 時代 之 大勢 不可 逆轉 亦 不必 畏懼

exercises.prompt: A reporter reads a mixed-register editorial line. Pick what you hear.
exercises.spokenText: 眾所周知，此次改革之於國民經濟，其影響之深遠，前所未有
options: 眾所周知，此次改革之於國民經濟，其影響之深遠，前所未有
大家都知道，這次改革對國民經濟的影響很深遠，史上沒有過
據說，這次改革對經濟影響很大，是頭一回
我們清楚，此次改革對經濟影響深遠，從未發生過
exercises.answer: 眾所周知，此次改革之於國民經濟，其影響之深遠，前所未有
exercises.explanation: All four classical particles stacked: 眾所周知 (所), 之於, 其, 之, 前所未有 (所). The other options paraphrase in modern colloquial or near-formal registers.

exercises.prompt: each classical particle to the modern function it performs in formal writing

pairs.right: Possessive / anaphoric (formal 它的 / 他的)
Coordinative / adversative connector (formal 並 / 但)

exercises.prompt: An editorial reads: "___ 周知，此次政策之於民生，其影響 ___ 深遠." Fill the all-knowing 所-construction (3 characters) and the modifier-link (1 character).
exercises.explanation: 眾所周知 + 之於 + 其影響 + 之深遠 — five classical particles in a single editorial sentence. The cluster is what marks 財新-style register.

exercises.prompt: In a modern editorial "其原因有三，此不可忽視", the 此 is functioning as:
options: A formal demonstrative pronoun (= 這 in elevated register)
exercises.answer: A formal demonstrative pronoun (= 這 in elevated register)
exercises.explanation: 此 is the literary counterpart of 這 — "this." Compare 此言 (this saying), 此事 (this matter), 由此可見 (from this we can see). It carries an editorial weight 這 doesn't.

lessons.title: 成語 in real context
lessons.description: Ten idioms, ten near-real headlines — pick the right fit

exercises.prompt: Headline: "創業三年終見曙光，張某 ___ 拿下千萬融資." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: After years of obscurity the founder astonishes everyone — exactly the 一鳴驚人 frame.

exercises.prompt: Editorial: "此次援助僅佔缺口的百分之一，對災區而言無異於 ___." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 1% of need = a cup of water on a burning cartload. The textbook "hopelessly insufficient" idiom.

exercises.prompt: Op-ed on a fallen executive: "___, 終遭法律嚴懲." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 見利忘義 = saw profit and forgot principle — the standard accusation aimed at corrupt executives.

exercises.prompt: Tech CEO at alma mater donation ceremony: "我之所以今日能站在這裡，無非是 ___." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 飲水思源 = drinking water, remembering its source. The conventional humble phrase for an alumnus giving back.

exercises.prompt: Friend missed a flight that later had a maintenance scare. You text: "哎，___, 看來反而是好事." Best fit?
exercises.explanation: 塞翁失馬，焉知非福 — bad luck that turns out to be good. The exact use case.

lessons.title: Which register is this?
lessons.description: Read the paragraph, name the register

exercises.prompt: "我方對此表示強烈不滿，並已就此向有關方面提出嚴正交涉." Register?
exercises.explanation: 我方 + 表示強烈不滿 + 有關方面 + 嚴正交涉 — four official-register markers in one sentence.

exercises.prompt: "據知情人士透露，截至發稿，公司方面尚無正式回應." Register?
exercises.explanation: 據知情人士透露 + 截至發稿 + 尚無回應 — the WSJ-style hedge cluster characteristic of 財新 / BBC中文 / 端傳媒.

exercises.prompt: "這波操作我給滿分，懂的都懂，233333." Register?
exercises.explanation: 這波操作 (sarcastic praise of a misstep) + 懂的都懂 (winking at censored topic) + 233333 (laughter). All three are unmistakable internet-satire markers.

exercises.prompt: "古人云讀萬卷書，行萬里路。此言至今猶存深意。綜上所述，唯有兼修，方能致遠." Register?
exercises.explanation: 古人云 opener + 綜上所述 pre-conclusion + 方能致遠 4-character closer. All three are 議論文 conventions.

exercises.prompt: "空山不見人，但聞人語響. 返景入深林，復照青苔上." Register?
options: Tang-poetry literary register (王維 in fact)
exercises.answer: Tang-poetry literary register (王維 in fact)
exercises.explanation: Five-character per line, classical particles, painterly imagery — Tang poetic register. (This is 王維's 鹿柴.)

exercises.prompt: "研究表明，長期使用社交媒體與青少年焦慮水平顯著相關." Register?
exercises.explanation: 研究表明 (citation hedge) + 顯著相關 (statistical-correlation jargon) + 社交媒體與焦慮水平 (technical noun phrase). Three academic-register markers in one sentence.

exercises.prompt: "咱這事兒吧，說大不大說小不小，先放放看唄." Register?
exercises.explanation: 咱 (northern "we"), 事兒 (er-suffix), 說大不大說小不小 (colloquial reduplication), 放放看唄 (final particle 唄). Four colloquial markers — unmistakably casual northern speech.

exercises.prompt: "既然你已經決定了，那就放手去做吧。無論結果如何，我都支援你." Register?
exercises.explanation: 既然 + 那就 + 無論…如何… + 我都 — formal connectors, but the rhythm is conversational and the second-person address is direct. Sits between casual and literary.

exercises.prompt: "是以本院駁回原告之訴訟請求." Register?
exercises.explanation: 是以 (formal 因此), 本院 (this court), 駁回 (legal verb "dismiss"), 之 (formal modifier-linker), 訴訟請求 (legal NP "plaint request"). Five judicial-register markers.

exercises.prompt: A reporter reads four sentences in different registers. Pick the one in independent / commercial-press hedge register.
exercises.spokenText: 據知情人士透露，截至發稿，公司方面尚無正式回應
options: 據知情人士透露，截至發稿，公司方面尚無正式回應
我方對此表示強烈不滿
這波操作我給滿分，懂的都懂

exercises.answer: 據知情人士透露，截至發稿，公司方面尚無正式回應
exercises.explanation: 據知情人士透露 + 截至發稿 + 尚無正式回應 — three commercial-press hedge markers (anonymous source, time-fence, unanswered-status). Distinct from official protest, online satire, and essay-quoted-authority registers.

lessons.title: Rhythm — fix the imbalanced parallel
lessons.description: Identify which clause breaks parallel weight, and rebuild it balanced

exercises.prompt: Which sentence keeps the cleanest parallel rhythm?
options: 一方面要兼顧效率，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要努力地兼顧整體效率，另一方面要保障公平。
一方面要兼顧效率，另一方面要切實地保障好社會公平。
一方面要兼顧效率問題，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.answer: 一方面要兼顧效率，另一方面要保障公平。
exercises.explanation: Both clauses are exactly 要 + 2-char verb + 2-char object. The other three pad one side and break the rhythm.

exercises.prompt: Which is the imbalanced clause in this pair: "成功也好，失敗這種事情其實也罷."
options: The first clause is too long
The second clause is padded — "這種事情其實" breaks the parallel with "成功"
exercises.answer: The second clause is padded — "這種事情其實" breaks the parallel with "成功"
exercises.explanation: 也好 / 也罷 demands matched short clauses. "成功 也好，失敗 也罷" — two characters each side. Anything more is padding.

exercises.prompt: Rewrite the imbalanced sentence into balanced parallel form: "Believe it or not, the facts are right there."
exercises.answer: 你 信 也好 不信 也罷 事實 就 在 那裡

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions of the same idea. Pick the one with the most balanced rhythm.
options: 與其在那裡抱怨，不如趕緊採取一些行動
與其抱怨，不如積極地採取一些有效的行動
與其去抱怨這件事情，不如行動
exercises.explanation: Two characters versus two characters. The padded versions all break the cadence — that's the C2 rhythm test.

exercises.prompt: Which of these parallel constructions is most balanced?
options: 效率 優先 ， 公平 為 本
效率 是 我們 應該 優先 考慮 的 ， 公平 為 本
效率 優先 ， 公平 也是 一個 非常 重要 的 價值
我們 要 重視 效率 ， 同時 也 要 兼顧 公平
exercises.answer: 效率 優先 ， 公平 為 本
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses with parallel grammar (NP + V/role). The other three pad one or both sides and break the cadence.

exercises.prompt: Build a balanced parallel pair: "Education roots the individual; education shapes the country."
exercises.answer: 教育 立 人 教育 興 國

exercises.prompt: A speaker reads four versions. Pick the one in balanced classical-flavored cadence.
exercises.spokenText: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
options: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
與其坐著空談各種道理，不如起來去採取行動
與其討論，不如趕快行動起來
與其在那裡討論道理，不如行動
exercises.answer: 與其坐而論道，不如起而行之
exercises.explanation: Two 4-character clauses, mirrored grammar (verb 而 verb-object). Classical-flavored 與其…不如… cadence at its most polished.

exercises.prompt: An editor flags this sentence as imbalanced: "我們應當傾聽民意，回應民憂." The most likely fix is:
options: Match the first clause's structure: "我們應當傾聽民意，我們應當回應民憂" (or both with 一方面 / 另一方面 framing)
exercises.answer: Match the first clause's structure: "我們應當傾聽民意，我們應當回應民憂" (or both with 一方面 / 另一方面 framing)
exercises.explanation: Original: 我們應當傾聽民意，回應民憂 — second clause drops 我們應當, breaking the parallel weight. The fix is to mirror the first clause's framing or use a parallel-pair connector. (Note: in some essay contexts the dropped second-clause subject is acceptable; the editor's call is style.)

exercises.prompt: Imbalanced: "成功也好，失敗這種事情其實也罷，過程才重要." Fix the second clause to match: "成功 也好 ， ___ 也罷 ， 過程 才 重要." Fill with 2 characters.
exercises.explanation: 也好…也罷 demands matched two-character clauses. The original's "失敗這種事情其實" is padding. The clean form is 成功也好，失敗也罷.

lessons.title: Dialogue: Editor reviewing a manuscript
lessons.description: Capstone — a literary editor walks an author through revisions.

exercises.prompt: Literary editor reviewing a novelist's draft

turns.speaker: su
turns.text: 稿子整體我讀完了，文氣貫通，但有幾處可商榷。(gǎo zi zhěng tǐ wǒ dú wán le, wén qì guàn tōng, dàn yǒu jǐ chù kě shāng què.)
turns.spokenText: 稿子整體我讀完了，文氣貫通，但有幾處可商榷。

turns.speaker: su
turns.text: 第二章開頭用了排比和反問，氣勢是有，但稍嫌雕琢。(dì èr zhāng kāi tóu yòng le pái bǐ hé fǎn wèn, qì shì shì yǒu, dàn shāo xián diāo zhuó.)
turns.spokenText: 第二章開頭用了排比和反問，氣勢是有，但稍嫌雕琢。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: The most diplomatic, register-appropriate author reply.
options: 您所言極是，我再斟酌字句，化雕琢為自然。(nín suǒ yán jí shì, wǒ zài zhēn zhuó zì jù, huà diāo zhuó wéi zì rán.)
隨便你怎麼改。(suí biàn nǐ zěn me gǎi.)
你不懂我的風格。(nǐ bù dǒng wǒ de fēng gé.)
我才不改。(wǒ cái bù gǎi.)
turns.answer: 您所言極是，我再斟酌字句，化雕琢為自然。(nín suǒ yán jí shì, wǒ zài zhēn zhuó zì jù, huà diāo zhuó wéi zì rán.)

turns.speaker: su
turns.text: 好態度。第五章人物對話夾了不少香港用語，臺灣讀者恐生疏。(hǎo tài du. dì wǔ zhāng rén wù duì huà jiā le bù shǎo xiāng gǎng yòng yǔ, tái wān dú zhě kǒng shēng shū.)
turns.spokenText: 好態度。第五章人物對話夾了不少香港用語，臺灣讀者恐生疏。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Which Hong Kong term might need a footnote for a mainland/Taiwan reader?
options: 茶餐廳 (chá cān tīng – HK-style diner)
turns.answer: 茶餐廳 (chá cān tīng – HK-style diner)

turns.speaker: su
turns.text: 茶餐廳雖通用，但情景要交代清。(chá cān tīng suī tōng yòng, dàn qíng jǐng yào jiāo dài qīng.)
turns.spokenText: 茶餐廳雖通用，但情景要交代清。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Fill the classical particle — "so-called" pattern: ___謂的盛世.
turns.answer: 所

turns.speaker: su
turns.text: 所謂的盛世——加引號，反諷自見。妙。(suǒ wèi de shèng shì — jiā yǐn hào, fǎn fěng zì xiàn. miào.)
turns.spokenText: 所謂的盛世——加引號，反諷自見。妙。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Pick the chengyu that best praises a manuscript as "polished and refined."
options: 字斟句酌 (zì zhēn jù zhuó – weighing every character)
粗製濫造 (cū zhì làn zào – shoddy production)
信口開河 (xìn kǒu kāi hé – speaking carelessly)
不知所云 (bù zhī suǒ yún – making no sense)
turns.answer: 字斟句酌 (zì zhēn jù zhuó – weighing every character)

turns.speaker: su
turns.text: 字斟句酌——正是我對您的期待。(zì zhēn jù zhuó — zhèng shì wǒ duì nín de qī dài.)
turns.spokenText: 字斟句酌——正是我對您的期待。

turns.speaker: you
turns.prompt: Finish the closing chengyu — "to put the finishing touch": 畫___點睛.
turns.answer: 龍

turns.speaker: su
turns.text: 畫龍點睛——再改一稿便可付梓。(huà lóng diǎn jīng — zài gǎi yī gǎo biàn kě fù zǐ.)
turns.spokenText: 畫龍點睛——再改一稿便可付梓。
